input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: The separator selection negates any_prefix_is_slash, picking ' / ' exactly when an option spelling already starts with a slash and '; ' otherwise.
- failure path: An option declared as --shout/--no-shout renders in --help as '--shout; --no-shout', and a Windows-style /debug;/no-debug option renders as '/debug / /no-debug', where the slash separator is indistinguishable from the slash prefix of the names.

Reviewer finding
- description: The separator logic was inverted during the refactor. The original code used `"; " if any_prefix_is_slash else " / "`, but the new code uses `"; " if not any_prefix_is_slash else " / "`.
- rationale: Trigger: any option with secondary opts, such as a boolean flag `--shout/--no-shout`. The original joined with " / " when no slash prefix was present and with "; " when one was. The new code swaps these, so help output changes from `--shout / --no-shout` to `--shout; --no-shout`. The same swap applies to slash-prefixed options. Every help page that lists such flags changes.
critique: The finding identifies the negated any_prefix_is_slash condition in the separator selection. It gives the same symptoms as the label: '--shout; --no-shout' for normal flags, and the reverse swap for slash-prefixed options. Mechanism and failure path match.
